## Effects

### Clock

```khora
pub effect Clock {
  unix_seconds: () -> Int,
  unix_millis: () -> Int,
  monotonic_millis: () -> Int,
  sleep: (Int) -> (),
}
```

What time it is.

A capability rather than plain functions, and separate from `Env` because
it is a different thing to deny: a library that may read a configuration
variable is not thereby a library that may know how long something took,
and a test that pins one usually wants to pin the other differently.

**Two clocks, not one, and the split is not a detail.** A wall clock says
what time it is and can jump: NTP steps it, an administrator sets it, a
virtual machine resumes with a stale one -- and it can jump *backwards*, so
subtracting two readings of it is not a duration, it is a guess. A
monotonic clock cannot go backwards and is what "how long did this take"
actually wants; its zero is arbitrary, so it can never be a timestamp.

One `millis` would therefore have been the wrong one about half the time,
and the half it was wrong for would be the half that only fails in
production, at 2am, when the clock is stepped an hour. Naming both makes
the caller say which they meant.
